chapter: Kansas City rooms and Piney Brown
title: Playing Dixieland with Bunk Johnson at the Yellow Front
summary: Lovett played with Bunk Johnson in Kansas City, not New Orleans, in the thirties; Bunk played Dixieland blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well tell me, when did you play with Bunk Johnson here in Kansas City?
Oh, that was way back -- way back, I guess about in the '30s.
Well, it's all way back.
Yeah, pretty far back and as I once said, we played at the Yellow Front.
That's right. Bunk Johnson played with you at the Yellow Front?
That's right.
Now you never played with Bunk down in New Orleans and down in Louisiana?
No.
Bunk played with you here in Kansas City?
That is right.

Now how did that New Orleans horn fit into your Kansas City jazz up here, because you played New Orleans drums I know, Louisiana drums. All you Louisiana drummers have that fabulous roll. I always catch that every-time from a Louisiana drummer but did Bunk fit in with the rest of the guys all right?
Oh yes, he played Dixie. We were playing Dixieland blues.
You were playing Dixie up here?
Yeah. You know, that's all Bunk knew from New Orleans. You know, he was born in New Orleans --
Oh yeah.
-- and --
Where was Kid Ory in those days, was he back in New Orleans?
Yeah, he was in New Orleans, yeah and--
George Lewis I guess he was down -- he didn't leave New Orleans until the '50s did he?
No, no.
Wouldn't go out on the road, never?
Couldn't get him away from there.
